## Layer 1 — Add and List

### What was hardest

*[First-person reflection on Layer 1. Possible threads: the Phase 1a+1b authoring back-and-forth between AI-suggested defaults and operator-specified constraints; the Phase 2a Red Gate discipline (and the documented scope-tradeoff that combined Phase 2a and 2b in one session, flagged in QE Review 1 Finding 1); the Phase 5 Surface A.0 cross-source purity-boundary divergence surfaced by SA Review 1; the Phase 5 Surface B cargo-mutants run that surfaced a missing falsifying test for the save-to-nested-path case (QE Review 2 Finding 1). The hardest single moment, the moment of realizing a defect that wasn't on any checklist, the part where the AI's default would have been wrong without operator pushback.]*

**AI-authored scaffold (Layer 1's hardest part from the AI's perspective):** The hardest part of Layer 1 from the AI agent's vantage was the Phase 5 Surface A.0 purity-boundary verification. The AI had authored `src/lib.rs:1-7` with a module-level doc comment claiming "Pure-core storage logic ... contains only pure functions"; the same AI had also authored `DESIGN.md` § Verification architecture with silence on per-function purity; and the same AI had authored an implementation where 3 of 4 `BookmarkStore` methods were effectful. The three artifacts were each defensible in isolation, but together they exhibited the cross-source divergence pattern G-173 names — and the AI hadn't seen it until SA Review 1 surfaced it in cold-context. The substantive lesson: an agent reviewing its own work normalizes the divergences it produced; the cross-source check (Surface A.0) is the discipline that catches what in-context inspection misses.

**This subsection requires director-authored prose to satisfy G-156.** See § AI-co-authored reference-example disclosure above.

### What I got wrong

*[First-person reflection on a specific mistake, agent-default that should have been rejected, decision that needed revisiting, or assumption that turned out to be wrong. Naming a specific mistake is the discipline; "everything went smoothly" is the anti-pattern.]*

**AI-authored scaffold:** The AI's initial Phase 2a Red Gate framing was wrong — the operator's directive to combine Phase 2a and Phase 2b into one demonstration session was an explicit scope tradeoff that the AI accepted without flagging as a Red Gate compliance issue. The eventual flag landed in QE Review 1 Finding 1 ("Phase 2a → 2b commit boundary not enforced") and was Resolved by documenting the tradeoff — but the documentation arrived AFTER the implementation, not at decision time. A director who genuinely owned the methodology would have surfaced the tradeoff before accepting the combined session; the AI deferred to the operator's framing without pushback. The lesson: AI-default-to-deference is itself a form of sycophancy that the VDD-IAR Alignment domain catches.

**This subsection requires director-authored prose to satisfy G-156.** See § AI-co-authored reference-example disclosure above.

### What the process felt like

*[First-person reflection on the process experience — what felt natural, what felt forced, what aspects of the methodology produced genuine insight vs. what felt like ceremony. The G-150 over-investment failure mode is harder to catch in-project than the under-investment one because more findings feel like more value; this subsection is the place to surface whether the methodology investment was proportionate.]*

**AI-authored scaffold:** The Phase 5 Surface B cargo-mutants run produced genuine signal — the 7/8 pre-fix kill rate revealing a missing falsifying test was a finding the AI would never have surfaced through inspection alone. The Phase 5 Surface A.0 purity-boundary verification produced the cross-source divergence finding which routed Raised-to-SO and re-shaped DESIGN.md. Both are examples of methodology-investment producing real findings. The opposite end — the rounds that produced only Hallucinated or zero findings (anticipated for many of PR 7's cold-session reviews on Layer 1) — would be the over-investment signal G-150 names. The honest accounting at Phase 6 will tally which rounds produced real findings vs. which were ceremony; that ratio is the methodology's calibration signal for the next project.

**This subsection requires director-authored prose to satisfy G-156.** See § AI-co-authored reference-example disclosure above.
